Priors for an areal model

Source: R/control.R
areal_priors.Rd

Priors are on the natural scale of each parameter. The field has precision \(\tau = 1/\sigma^2\); the fixed effects are integrated out analytically, so their prior must be Gaussian.

Usage

areal_priors(
  sigma_sd = 2,
  rho_s = c(2, 1),
  rho_t = c(1, 1),
  sigma_n_sd = 1,
  beta_mean = 0,
  beta_sd = 3
)

Arguments

sigma_sd

Scale of the half-normal prior on sigma, the scale of the space-time field: \(\sigma \sim N^+(0, \code{sigma\_sd}^2)\).

rho_s

Shape parameters of the Beta prior on rho_s, the spatial dependence of the Leroux prior (0: independent areas, 1: intrinsic CAR). The default Beta(2, 1) favours strong spatial dependence.

rho_t

Shape parameters of the Beta prior on rho_t, the lag-one correlation of the AR1 in time. Default uniform. With one time step the data say nothing about rho_t, and its posterior is this prior.

sigma_n_sd

Scale of the half-normal prior on sigma_n, the standard deviation of the cell-level nugget.

beta_mean, beta_sd

Means and standard deviations of the independent normal priors on the fixed effects (logit scale). Give one value (used for every fixed effect), one value per fixed effect in the order of the design, or a vector named by design column, e.g. c(intercept = 0, rain = 0), where unnamed columns take the default. The design columns are the intercept, trend (if trend() is in the formula), then the covariates in the order of the formula, a factor giving one column per level after the first (named by the covariate and the level, e.g. zonehigh). They are listed in fit$design$names.

Value

A list of the settings.

Details

fit_areal() also accepts a plain list of any of these arguments, e.g. priors = list(sigma_sd = 1); the others take their defaults.

Examples

areal_priors()
#> $sigma_sd
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $rho_s
#> [1] 2 1
#> 
#> $rho_t
#> [1] 1 1
#> 
#> $sigma_n_sd
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $beta_mean
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $beta_sd
#> [1] 3
#> 
areal_priors(sigma_sd = 1, rho_t = c(4, 1))
#> $sigma_sd
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $rho_s
#> [1] 2 1
#> 
#> $rho_t
#> [1] 4 1
#> 
#> $sigma_n_sd
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $beta_mean
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $beta_sd
#> [1] 3
#>
